description: Model families that appear in the imported corpus. This is deliberately separate from prompts/models.json: that registry covers the nine models the curated scenes are written for, with label formats and per-model prompt structure. This one covers every family present in the imported data, and records how well each family's capabilities are actually verified.

verificationLevels.vendor-documented: Capabilities read from vendor documentation or the vendor's own repository on 2026-10-20.
verificationLevels.third-party-only: The model name appears in third-party prompt collections; no vendor page was retrievable to confirm capabilities.
verificationLevels.unverified: Present in the corpus but neither vendor-documented nor described by a source this project trusts.

families.name: Seedance
families.note: Seedance 2.5 raises the ceiling to 30 s and accepts up to 30 images / 10 videos / 10 audio clips as references.

families.name: Kling
families.durations: 3–15 s (3.0 tiers); 5 or 10 s (2.5 Turbo Pro)
families.note: Kling 3.0 Standard / Pro / 4K are documented. `kling-4.0` appears in 12 imported prompts from a third-party collection but is NOT listed on the vendor model page consulted on 2026-10-20 — treat those prompts as retrospective unless you can see the model in your own account.

families.name: Veo
families.durations: 4 / 6 / 8 s per clip; +7 s per extension
families.note: Audio is generated on every request; there is no documented negative-prompt parameter.

families.name: Wan
families.note: 3.0 and 3.0 Prime list built-in audio. 2.7 accepts an `audio_url` to replace generated sound.

families.name: MiniMax H3 / Hailuo
families.note: The vendor page documents audio as an *input* reference (up to 3 clips, ≤15 s total). It does not state whether generated output carries an audio track, so `nativeAudio: true` here is an inference from the third-party corpus, not a vendor claim.

families.name: Sora 2
families.durations: 4 / 8 / 12 s, up to 20 s; extensions to 120 s
families.note: The Videos API shut down on 2026-09-24 with no one-to-one replacement. These prompts are archival.

families.name: Runway Gen-4 / Aleph
families.note: Aleph adds edit verbs (add / remove / change / replace / re-light / re-style); Gen-4 is text-to-video. No native audio.

families.name: HappyHorse 1.0
families.resolutions: not stated by the vendor model list
families.note: Corpus median is 35 words, the shortest of any family. Audio is listed as built-in.

families.name: Gemini Omni Flash
families.durations: not stated by the vendor model list
families.resolutions: not stated by the vendor model list
families.note: Accepted as an instruction-style, iterable surface.

families.name: HunyuanVideo
families.note: The base model generates no audio. HunyuanVideo-Avatar is audio-*driven* (audio in, not out) — a different variant, not a capability of the base model.

families.name: CogVideoX
families.note: Frame counts follow 16N+1 (1.5) or 8N+1 (2B/5B). No audio generation is documented.

families.name: LTX-Video / LTX-2
families.durations: up to 60 s (LTX-Video 13B long-shot); up to 10 s with synchronized audio (LTX-2)
families.resolutions: up to 4K at 50 FPS; default 1216x704 at 30 FPS
families.note: Audio belongs to LTX-2, not the earlier LTX-Video releases. The repository describes LTX-2 as the audio-video model; do not assume the 13B long-shot build generates sound.

families.name: Mochi 1
families.durations: not stated (API example uses 31 frames, no frame rate given)
families.note: Duration cannot be derived from the vendor material available on 2026-10-20; the frame count alone is not a duration without a frame rate.

families.name: Luma Ray
families.note: The corpus names `luma-ray-3.2`. The vendor documentation consulted on 2026-10-20 lists Ray 2 and Ray 2 Flash only, so the 3.2 naming is unconfirmed.

families.name: 即梦 / Jimeng
families.note: No vendor documentation was retrievable on 2026-10-20. Every claim in the corpus about this family is third-party.

families.name: Pika
families.note: The vendor docs endpoint did not respond on 2026-10-20. The corpus's 91% negative-constraint rate reflects the `no morphing` convention, not a vendor requirement.

families.name: Higgsfield
families.note: The product site describes Genjutsu as motion transfer and object swapping but publishes no per-model duration or audio spec.
